title: Cohomology of abelian sheaves on a finite-dimensional spectral space
statement:
Let $T$ be a spectral topological space [def-weil-spectral-space], let $d\geq0$ be an integer, and suppose its topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] is at most $d$. For every sheaf $F$ of abelian groups on $T$, with cohomology the right-derived global sections in abelian sheaves [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology],
$$H^q(T,F)=0\qquad(q>d).$$
The empty space is included, with dimension $-\infty$. No Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0A3G, proposition-cohomological-dimension-spectral, part (1) (lines 3940–3948); with an upper bound d in place of the exact dimension.

proof.text: We may apply the cited ringed-space lemmas to abelian sheaves as follows. On any space $Y$ give every abelian sheaf its canonical module structure over the constant integer sheaf $\underline{\mathbf Z}_Y$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]: an integer acts by repeated addition, and a locally constant integer section acts by gluing these operations on opens where it is constant. Conversely any such module structure is forced by the action of $1$. Every additive sheaf map respects this action. Thus forgetting this structure and supplying it back are inverse on objects and maps, commute with sections and open restriction, and preserve injectivity because their lifting problems are identical. Computing the two cohomologies on the same injective resolution identifies the ringed-space cohomology [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology] with the abelian-sheaf cohomology [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology], including the restriction maps. In the remaining steps, ringed-space citations always use this integer structure.

source.place: Section 01DZ, equations defining abelian-sheaf and module-sheaf cohomology; canonical integer-module convention for the lemmas used in Tag 0A3G.

proof.text: For the empty space all sheaf sections, hence all terms of a global-sections resolution, are zero. This proves the stated empty case in every degree. For nonempty spaces we prove simultaneously by induction on $n\geq0$: (A$_n$) for every spectral $X$ with $\dim X\leq n$ and every abelian sheaf $F$, $H^q(X,F)=0$ for $q>n$; and (B$_n$) for the same $X,F$ and every quasi-compact open $U\subseteq X$, restriction $H^n(X,F)\to H^n(U,F|_U)$ is surjective. Both assertions are also retained for the empty space. This is an induction on an upper bound, so it applies directly to the given $d$; there is no assumption that $\dim X=d$.

source.place: Tag 0A3G, opening induction on dimension, phrased with upper bounds.

proof.text: For $n=0$ and $X$ nonempty, there are no nontrivial specializations. Indeed, if $x$ specializes to $y\ne x$, the irreducible closed sets $\overline{\{y\}}\subsetneq\overline{\{x\}}$ give a chain of length one, contradicting $\dim X\leq0$; strictness follows from sobriety, hence the $T_0$ property. Thus $\overline{\{x\}}=\{x\}$ for every $x$: the set $X^c$ of closed points is all of $X$, in particular closed, and its subspace topology is that of $X$. Clause 1 of [det-pe-wlocal-components], applied with $T=X$, says that $X^c=X$ is profinite: compact, Hausdorff and totally disconnected. Then [lem-cbc-profinite-topological-cohomology-vanishing] gives (A$_0$). Every quasi-compact open $U$ is a compact subset of the Hausdorff space $X$, hence closed, so $U$ is clopen. A section of $F$ on $U$ extends by the zero section on $X\setminus U$, using the sheaf gluing axiom for the disjoint open covering $X=U\sqcup(X\setminus U)$. This proves (B$_0$).

source.place: Tag 0A3G, base case; Topology Tag 0905 (lemma-characterize-profinite-spectral, (5)⇒(1)) through det-pe-wlocal-components clause 1, and Cohomology Tag 0A3F.

proof.text: Let $n\geq1$, assume (A$_{n-1}$) and (B$_{n-1}$) for all spectral spaces of dimension at most $n-1$, and fix $X,F$ with $\dim X\leq n$. To prove (B$_n$), let $U\subseteq X$ be quasi-compact open and $\xi\in H^n(U,F|_U)$. Set $Z=X\setminus U$, $W=\{x:\overline{\{x\}}\cap Z\ne\varnothing\}$ and $S=W\setminus Z$. The hypotheses of [lem-sfb-punctured-spectral-neighborhood-dimension] hold: $Z$ is closed and its open complement is exactly the quasi-compact $U$. Thus $S$ is spectral of dimension at most $n-1$. Applying (A$_{n-1}$) to $F|_S$ in degree $n$ yields $H^n(S,F|_S)=0$. The case $S=\varnothing$ uses the empty case already proved.

source.place: Tag 0A3G, induction step proving (2), punctured generalization neighborhood.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-punctured-neighborhood-cohomology-colimit] to this closed $Z$ and its quasi-compact open complement. Its indexing category consists of the quasi-compact open neighborhoods $N$ of $Z$, with reverse inclusion; it is small (a set of subsets of $X$), nonempty (contains $X$), and directed (intersections are quasi-compact). The class $\xi$ is at the stage $N=X$, since $X\setminus Z=U$. Its image in the colimit is zero by the preceding step and the comparison isomorphism to $H^n(S,F|_S)$. The filtered-colimit zero criterion [lem-sc-filtered-colimit-map-zero] gives a quasi-compact open neighborhood $V$ of $Z$ at which this class vanishes: $\xi|_{V\setminus Z}=0$. Here $V\setminus Z=V\cap U$.

source.place: Tag 0A3G, induction step proving (2), displayed colimit and shrinking V; Tag 0A3D(2).

proof.text: Since $Z\subseteq V$, the opens $U,V$ cover $X$. The pair $(\xi,0)\in H^n(U,F|_U)\oplus H^n(V,F|_V)$ restricts to zero under the difference map to $H^n(U\cap V,F|_{U\cap V})$, by the preceding step. The exact Mayer–Vietoris sequence [lem-sc-mayer-vietoris-ringed-space], applied with the integer coefficients of step 1, therefore supplies $\widetilde\xi\in H^n(X,F)$ restricting to $(\xi,0)$. In particular it restricts to $\xi$ on $U$. This proves (B$_n$) before it is used to prove (A$_n$).

source.place: Tag 0A3G, conclusion of the proof of (2), using Tag 01EB.

proof.text: Choose an injective resolution $0\to F\to I^0\to I^1\to\cdots$ in abelian sheaves, using [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaves-enough-injectives] on the site of opens and the resolution definition [def-sp-injective-resolutions], and set $G=\ker(I^n\to I^{n+1})=\operatorname{im}(I^{n-1}\to I^n)$. The latter equality uses exactness of the resolution and $n\geq1$. Kernels of sheaves are computed on sections, so for every open $A\subseteq X$ the degree-$n$ cycles are $G(A)$. Restricting the injective resolution to $A$ remains an injective resolution by [lem-sc-ringed-space-restrict-injective-resolution] and step 1. Consequently the definition of degree-$n$ cohomology gives the exact row $I^{n-1}(A)\to G(A)\to H^n(A,F|_A)\to0$. These rows for $A=X,U$ form a commuting restriction diagram, because all their maps are induced by the same differential and restriction maps.

source.place: Tag 0A3G, proof of (1) assuming (2), definition of G and displayed diagram; Tag 01E1 for restriction of resolutions.

proof.text: For a quasi-compact open $U\subseteq X$ and $g\in G(U)$, let $c$ be its image in $H^n(U,F|_U)$. By (B$_n$), lift $c$ to $\widetilde c\in H^n(X,F)$ and then, by exactness of the top row, to $h\in G(X)$. The difference $g-h|_U$ maps to zero in $H^n(U,F|_U)$, hence equals the differential of some $b\in I^{n-1}(U)$. The injective-sheaf restriction theorem [lem-weil-pbc-injective-sheaf-mono-restriction], on the small site of opens of $X$, lifts $b$ to $\widetilde b\in I^{n-1}(X)$; the inclusion $U\hookrightarrow X$ is a monomorphism. Then $h+d\widetilde b$ restricts to $g$. Thus $G(X)\to G(U)$ is surjective for every quasi-compact open $U$. If $U\subseteq V$ are both quasi-compact open, this also makes $G(V)\to G(U)$ surjective: first lift to $X$, then restrict to $V$.

source.place: Tag 0A3G, diagram chase using flasqueness of I^{n-1}; injective restriction Tag 01EA.

proof.text: The quasi-compact opens of $X$ form a basis stable under binary intersections by spectrality. The surjectivities just proved therefore satisfy every hypothesis of [lem-sfb-quasi-compact-restriction-acyclicity], so $G$ is acyclic for global sections (take $V=X$, which is quasi-compact). The exact augmented complex $0\to F\to I^0\to\cdots\to I^{n-1}\to G\to0$ is a resolution in degrees $0,\ldots,n$; its earlier terms are injective and hence acyclic by part 1 of [lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity]. Apply part 2 of that lemma to global sections on abelian sheaves, whose source category has enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaves-enough-injectives]; the target abelian groups have enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-modules-enough-injectives] with $R=\mathbf Z$, since the integer action is uniquely determined by the additive group. It identifies $H^q(X,F)$ with the degree-$q$ cohomology of $I^0(X)\to\cdots\to I^{n-1}(X)\to G(X)$. This complex has zero terms above degree $n$, hence zero cohomology there. This proves (A$_n$), closes the simultaneous induction, and taking $n=d$ proves the item.

source.place: Tag 0A3G, proof of (1) assuming (2), acyclicity of G and truncated acyclic resolution; Tags 0A36, 01EW, 015E.

tool_uses.why: Clause 1 (closed points of a spectral space with closed closed-point locus form a profinite subspace) gives profiniteness of a zero-dimensional spectral space in the induction base; no node of the unit gives it.
The profinite topological vanishing theorem supplies the induction base; it is a generic cohomology input rather than a replacement of the compactification unit route.
The canonical cohomology comparison on punctured generalization neighborhoods is the continuity tool used in Stacks 0A3G; our unit contains no substitute.
Detects a zero class at a finite stage in a filtered colimit of groups; purely algebraic tool.
Exactness for a two-open cover glues a class with zero; use the constant integer ringed space, as justified in step 1.
Allows the same injective resolution to compute on every open; a generic ringed-space tool with integer coefficients.
Supplies surjectivity of sections of an injective sheaf along an open inclusion; a generic site tool.
Computes global cohomology from the finite resolution by acyclic sheaves; a generic derived-functor tool.
Provides actual existence of an injective resolution on the small site of opens, rather than inferring existence from a definition.
Checks the enough-injectives hypothesis on the target category of global sections, specializing modules to the integers.
